subject: live README hero widget
activeForm: Building the live README hero and its click-through funnel
description:
Status: CARDED, not started. Successor to the static screenshot hero shipped by
`specs/001-readme-landing/`.

## Idea

The README hero becomes a live view of the service with a zero-friction path into it.
GitHub's sanitizer strips script, iframe, style, and event handlers from READMEs and
proxies every image through camo, so true embedded interactivity is impossible. The
workable shape:

1. A new unauthenticated route on the dashboard Lambda renders current sentiment plus
   price for one ticker as an SVG, `Cache-Control: no-cache`. Camo forwards the origin
   cache headers, so every README view refetches: the hero is live data on every load
   (the github-readme-stats mechanism).
2. The README wraps that image in a link to the deployed customer dashboard, which
   already mints a guest session on cold load with no sign-in. Visitor sees live data,
   clicks, and is interacting with the real app in one step.
3. Funnel, not a rope: guest first, and sign-up (account, alerts) only when they
   already like it.

## Constraints learned up front

- No JS, no iframe, no widget import in READMEs. Image plus link is the ceiling.
- The render route is public and unauthenticated: rate-limit it, keep user data out,
  expect scrapers.
- Lambda cold start sits on the first-impression path; consider provisioned
  concurrency or a tiny render cache with short TTL.
- Preprod daily sentiment is one article per ticker per day (every 24h bucket has
  count 1), so the drawn series is spiky; pick the ticker and window that read best,
  or render the aggregated line the dashboard itself shows.
- Decide which URL is public before shipping the link (preprod Amplify vs prod).

## Also in scope when picked up

Formalize the one-off hero capture (`hero_capture.mjs`, scratchpad) as a guarded e2e
spec so every suite run regenerates the static fallback screenshot for free. Guard it
behind an env flag so CI cannot fail on it. The GIF stub in the README
(`<!-- GRAPHIC STUB -->`) is retired by this feature too: a live hero plus a real
capture makes the animated GIF redundant.

## Carried from PI-RESUME-live-hero-widget.md (2026-08-12)

- Commissioned verbatim by the operator 2026-08-05 as item 3 of three: e2e node fix (shipped, PR #1031), then signed-sentiment-fanout battleplan (card 1), then live-hero-widget "also battleplan with research component". No spec, plan or research artifacts exist yet; only this card.
- Sequencing: a good hero needs card 1 landed first. Today every mode renders an identical line pinned near +1.0, which is exactly the defect card 1 fixes.
- 1Y is impossible: sentiment history is capped at roughly 90d by TTL, so 3M is the deepest full-coverage range.
- Dashboard trap (AGENTS.md): the render route goes on the dashboard Lambda (admin stack, vanilla JS side); the click-through target is the CUSTOMER dashboard at https://main.d29tlmksqcx494.amplifyapp.com/.
- Standing constraint: no new AWS resources without asking, which binds the render-cache decision.
- hero_capture.mjs lived in session 720d139a's scratchpad and may be gone; it used createRequire against frontend/package.json and ran the non-mocked flow against the Amplify URL.
